programme.title: Ardal O'Hanlon: Tomb Raider
programme.desc: The actor explores some of the most important archaeological finds in Ireland's history, revealing how many have been used as an important tool for nation-building on both sides of the border. Speaking to world-renowned experts, he unravels a forgotten time period, when a team of Americans from Harvard University, a Nazi archaeologist from Austria, and a Welsh geography professor dug up ancient sites across the country. Their pioneering work answered questions about the Celts, and what it means to be Irish

programme.title: Kamikaze: An Untold History
programme.desc: On the Pacific front, towards the end of the Second World War, Japan's imperial armed forces launched kamikaze attacks - suicide missions by aircraft laden with bombs. Close to 4,000 Japanese airmen died, and nearly 7,000 Allied military personnel were killed, and thousands more were injured by the attacks. How could this happen? Utilising 15 years' worth of extensive interviews with US and Japanese veterans, Takayuki Oshima's film delves into the mechanism of how a crazed madness swept through an entire nation

programme.title: The Sky at Night
programme.desc: Professor Brian Cox joins the team to explore the mysteries of black holes in light of the James Webb Space Telescope's most exciting new observations, which has upended everything scientists thought they knew about black holes and the evolution of the universe itself

programme.title: The Wildest Weather in the Universe: Horizon
programme.desc: Documentary following scientists conducting research into weather on other planets, using unmanned spacecraft to study the solar system and the latest telescopes to examine distant worlds. Their findings have revealed strange phenomena including rains of precious stones, supersonic winds, storms that encompass entire worlds, and temperatures so hot that the clouds are formed of lava

programme.title: Beautiful Equations
programme.desc: Artist and critic Matt Collings explores the world of mathematical equations, looking at some of the most famous examples in science, including Einstein's Emc2 and Newton's laws of gravity. Along the way he meets Stephen Hawking to talk about black holes, looks up at the planets at an observatory in Cambridge, observes a particle of anti-matter, and sees how the concepts of beauty and elegance have been used by scientists to advance their work

programme.title: World's Ultimate Adventures
programme.desc: Chef and content creator Julie Lin is on a Turkish adventure - combining her passion for food with history. Travelling through the south east, known as the gastronomic heart, she first stops in the city of Gazianetep - world famous for its baklava. Julie uncovers what makes this delicacy and the locally grown pistachios inside it so special. Heading further east, she visits the Neolithic site of Karahan Tepe, a discovery so significant that it is reshaping our understanding of human history. Guided by the archaeological team, Julie explores their latest finds, including what may be the world's oldest kitchen. Her journey ends in ?anl?urfa, cooking with a family keeping traditional recipes alive, discovering the city's signature smoked pepper, and finishing her trip with a vibrant cultural, night-time celebration and an unusual raw-meat dish.

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: It's harvest time for Andy and Jo in Fife as they finally reap what they have down - and after a challenging year it remains to be seen what the wet weather might have cost them. Nick and Holly diversify with a new cattle venture in Dumfries, and the Bakers on Papa Westray take delivery of a milking cow and calf to add to their ever-growing family

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Brian Cunningham's beginner's guide to vegetable growing started in April, and now it's time to reap the rewards as he starts to harvest from the veg plot. Calum Clunie starts the sowing cycle again in his family sized plot as he sows for winter crops

programme.title: Paramedics on Scene
programme.desc: In Glasgow, Paul and Ryan of the Special Operations Response Team are called to a siege in a flat, where a man has barricaded himself inside and is threatening to harm himself. Meanwhile, Aberdeen-based crewmates Kirsty and Bruce are called to see Rebecca, who has suffered a severe anaphylactic attack, but she shows little sign of improvement after several doses of adrenaline, prompting a rapid journey on blue-lights to Aberdeen Royal Infirmary

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: My Kind of Town
programme.desc: Ian Hamilton and his dog Major head to Cupar in Fife, a traditional market town that now has ambitions to be a digital hub. Ian gets the chance to practise his swing on the Kingarrock Hickory golf course and samples some tasty morsels at the farmers' market

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: The autumn sales are over and preparations are being made for winter. In Newtonmore in Cairngorms National Park, Robert MacKenzie needs to gather in all his cows back down to the croft for pregnancy testing, while on North Uist, the MacDonalds are harvesting potatoes grown in the sandy machair soil unique to the west of Scotland

programme.title: Murder Trial: Death of a Dog Walker
programme.desc: Part one of two. Former gamekeeper David Campbell stands accused of the premeditated murder of Brian Low, a 65-year-old groundsman on the same estate where they both worked. With the site of the murder exposed to the elements for days, police are unable to forensically link anyone to the deceased, so the prosecution build a case against the accused around smaller, individual strands of circumstantial evidence, while working to convince the jury that he's guilty beyond reasonable doubt

programme.title: David Wilson's Crime Files
programme.desc: The criminologist discusses the use of forensic science in crime detection, looking at its 19th-century origins and more recent use in unresolved murder cases that are decades old

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Discussion on Scotland's biggest news stories, with Martin Geissler, Laura Miller and Natalie Higgins

programme.title: Icons of Football
programme.desc: A profile of former Celtic, Barcelona and Sweden striker Henrik Larsson, who reflects on his upbringing in the city of Helsingborg and early promise at Hgaborg and Helsingborgs, and his difficult years at Feyenoord, where game time and confidence wavered. The programme charts his transformation at Celtic, where he became the defining player of an era, before his story as a player culminated in Spain, where he joined Barcelona and played a decisive role in their 2006 Champions League triumph. With contributions by Martin O'Neill, Chris Sutton, Johan Mjllby, Paul Lambert and Regi Blinker

programme.title: Reporting Scotland: News at Seven
programme.desc: Reports from BBC newsrooms across the country with analysis and discussion on the big stories of the day

programme.title: Hidden Lives
programme.desc: Presenter Vonny LeClerc delves into the fast and furious world of female roller derby, finding a sport that is an expression of femininity and sisterhood

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: George Anderson and Brian Cunningham tackle viewers' questions and also start a major new project as they launch a makeover of an area at Beechgrove called the Crooked Garden. One of the first parts of that revamp is the creation of a stumpery, a growing technique based on an old tree and planted with a range of ferns. George has details on feeding cherry trees right now, Brian is back in the 8x6 greenhouse, and there is a visit to St Andrews Botanic Garden

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: Three getaways that didn't fit into any of this year's categories are judged as part of wildcard week, with Kirsty and Helen from Perthshire rating Monachyle Mhor in the Trossachs, House of Gods hotel in Edinburgh, and Glen Dye, a 15,000-acre private estate in Aberdeenshire

programme.title: Martin Compston's Scottish Fling
programme.desc: The Line of Duty star travels across his homeland with his best friend and TV presenter Phil MacHugh to see how its people and landscape are shaping the country. Their journey begins in Martin's hometown of Greenock, where Phil has arranged some unexpected transport across the water to sunny Dunoon. Here the boys indulge in an end-of-the-pier snapshot of the traditional seaside holiday Martin experienced as a boy - crazy golf and ice cream with a not-so-traditional local, BBC's Drag Race winner Lawrence Chaney

programme.title: Martin Compston's Scottish Fling
programme.desc: The actor is given a taste of island life when his friend Phil MacHugh takes him on a journey back to his family's homeland of the Western Isles. Iin Stornoway, they have an appointment at the barbers to meet Syrian refugee Ousama and his eldest son Abdullah to see how their family have been settling into Western Isle life

programme.title: Scot Squad
programme.desc: Singh and McKirdy gallantly help out a hen do and the Chief attempts international diplomacy by shouting loudly at a laptop. Newly promoted PC Ken Beattie now finds himself called upon to provide a character reference

programme.title: Edinburgh Unlocked
programme.desc: Mark Nelson is back with a selection of the best of the Edinburgh Festival, featuring the pick of the comedy, music, cabaret and theatre from all over the world

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Discussion on Scotland's biggest news stories, with Martin Geissler, Laura Miller and Natalie Higgins

programme.title: Growing Up Scottish
programme.desc: Scotland's comedians look back at friendship, bonding, BFFs and sleepovers. Then there is a look at homes - the flats and the crofts, the bathrooms and the controversial inside/outside toilets

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news

programme.title: Spud
programme.desc: Very average woman Spud cooks, cleans, serves and cares for her father. The only problem is she does it all rather badly - and half-heartedly. A woman who is never seen, unattractive and ignored, she does not feel bad about herself. However, when her father dies, she starts to realise she may have to come out from the shadow and be seen. Comedy drama, written by and starring Siobhn McSweeney

programme.title: Lara Croft: Tomb Raider
programme.desc: The gun-toting treasure seeker is thrown into a furious battle with a mysterious secret society as she races against time to locate the missing pieces of a legendary artefact that grants the owner the ability to control time. Action adventure based on the video games, starring Angelina Jolie, Daniel Craig, Leslie Phillips, Iain Glen, Chris Barrie and Jon Voight

programme.title: RuPaul's Drag Race UK: Meet the Queens
programme.desc: RuPaul introduces the 12 queens competing for the coveted title of the UK's next drag race superstar

programme.title: Bridget Jones's Diary
programme.desc: A single woman begins a new year with resolutions to find love, quit her bad habits and take a step up the career ladder. Her plans crumble as she tries to deal with her mother's infidelity, get over a passionate fling with her boss and come to terms with her feelings for an uptight lawyer. Romantic comedy based on Helen Fielding's novel, starring Renee Zellweger, Hugh Grant and Colin Firth

programme.title: Bridget Jones: The Edge of Reason
programme.desc: The disaster-prone journalist seems to have finally found the perfect boyfriend. However, when the couple start to squabble over their personal habits, she decides to decamp for a while to Thailand and write a travelogue. Unfortunately, she has reckoned without the reappearance of a duplicitous old flame - and a spell behind bars in a Thai prison. Romantic comedy sequel, with Renee Zellweger, Colin Firth, Hugh Grant, Jim Broadbent and Gemma Jones

programme.title: Matthew Perry and the Ketamine Queen
programme.desc: Amber Haque explores the relationship between the Friends actor and Los Angeles-based drug dealer and dual US-UK citizen Jasveen Sangha - dubbed the Ketamine Queen by US prosecutors - who was one of five people charged in connection with Perry's untimely death, including two doctors and Perry's personal assistant. She pleaded guilty to five federal counts, including one of distributing ketamine resulting in death

programme.title: Stacey Dooley: Ready for War?
programme.desc: The reporter follows a group of Ukrainian civilians as they arrive in the UK for five weeks of intensive army training before deployment to the frontline fighting against Russia. Among the group is florist and gardener Mykola who wants to join his family members on the frontline and fight towards victory so he can marry his girlfriend. For Pasha, a welder who was living abroad when the invasion began, he fears going into battle means never seeing his parents again

programme.title: My Mate's a Bad Date
programme.desc: Twenty-five-year-old Mancunian Tyler is a self-confessed serial dater who treats dating like a sport and goes on five or six dates a week. She's rude and sarcastic, rambles on about herself, gets bored easily and doesn't stay focused on her dates. Here, she wants to find the male version of herself, so Oloni puts that idea to the test by setting her up on three challenging dates

programme.title: Stacey Dooley: Blood, Sweat and T-Shirts
programme.desc: Six teenagers learn where their clothes have come from, travelling to India to see first-hand the textiles industry that churns out designer-wear for Western consumers like themselves. As the group experience life in these workshops, the stress of life where employees literally eat and sleep by their machines becomes too much for one - and that is before they learn about their wages

programme.title: The Catch Up
programme.desc: A round-up of the day's news

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Part two of two. Steve Backshall continues his adventure in the Philippines, where he swims with one of the deadliest snakes on the planet, meets a shark that spends most of its time more than 500 metres underwater, and searches in the jungle for a tarsier - a predator that eats its victims head-first

programme.title: Deadly 60
programme.desc: Steve Backshall takes a close look at dogs and their distant relatives, wolves. He heads to the Arctic Circle where a pack of huskies show him a thing or two about stamina. Steve is then rescued by an avalanche dog whose incredible nose sniffs him out from deep beneath the snow. Finally he comes face-to-face with one of his favourite animals, the wolf.

programme.title: Sort Your Life Out with Stacey Solomon
programme.desc: The team help the Jamiesons from East Sussex transform the home that's been in their family for 40 years. programme.desc: Kilmarnock v Celtic (Kick-off 1.30pm). Coverage of the Scottish Premiership match from The BBSP Stadium Rugby Park. The Bhoys will be looking to extend a run of eight consecutive wins against Killie, which dates back to May 2024, and includes two victories here in the previous campaign. The most recent of those matches in February looked to be going in favour of the hosts when Tyreece John-Jules and Joe Hugill gave Kilmarnock a 2-0 lead at half-time, only for Sebastian Tounekti, Benjamin Nygren, and Julian Araujo to turn things around and give Martin O'Neill a victory in his 300th game in charge of the Glasgow club

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: Notts County v Leicester City (Kick-off 12.00pm). Coverage of the League One match at Meadow Lane. It has been a turbulent few years for Leicester, who have endured financial difficulties and been relegated in each of the last two seasons. In contrast, the Magpies were playing non-league football three seasons ago, but have been promoted twice since then to reach the third tier for the first time since the 2014/15 campaign

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: York City v Bristol Rovers (Kick-off 3.00pm). Coverage of both teams' opening League Two match of the season, held at LNER Community Stadium. York won the National League last term to secure a place in the Football League since they were relegated in the 2015/16 season, but their title-winning manager Stuart Maynard departed during the summer and was replaced by Scott Lindsey. Their opponents will be looking to improve on last season's 14th-place finish and push for promotion

programme.title: Live EFL
programme.desc: Sheffield United v Birmingham City (kick-off 5.30pm). Coverage of both teams' opening match of the Championship season, held at Bramall Lane. United claimed a 3-0 win in last season's corresponding fixture thanks to goals by Tyler Bindon, Gustavo Hamer and Patrick Bamford, but Birmingham were reduced to 10 men in the 18th minute due to Tommy Doyle's red card when the score was 1-0

programme.title: Live: European Athletics Championships
programme.desc: Coverage from the night session on the second day of the event, which takes place at Alexander Stadium in Birmingham, including the men's 100m final. Italy's Marcel Jacobs has established himself as one of the greatest sprinters the continent has ever produced over the years, winning this title in 2022 and 2024 and also taking Olympic gold in Tokyo, but the British trio of Romell Glave, Jeremiah Azu and Louie Hinchcliffe will hope to have qualified and to provide Jacobs with stiff competition. The women's 5,000m is the first final of the night, and also taking place are the men's long jump and women's 100m hurdles finals, which saw Greece's Miltiadis Tentoglou and Cyrna Samba-Mayela of France break the respective championship records two years ago in Rome
